title: Closing line after a reflection
what: A blue to peach gradient with one centred line: Reflecting can bring up a lot. Treat yourself tenderly today, and come back here anytime. A single white Done button.
takeaway: One kind sentence on a quiet full screen is enough after a heavy entry; it names that feelings may surface and leaves the door open.

title: Daily reflection after a very unpleasant day
what: A sad purple star mascot over the title Daily reflection and the line You noted feeling Very Unpleasant on January 20th. Could any of these tasks have played a role? Below are three completed tasks with plus buttons.
takeaway: After a low mood, ask a gentle question that links it to the day instead of judging it; the user can tag causes in one tap.

title: Are you in crisis
what: Heading Are you in crisis? You are not alone. Help is just a call away. Two outlined helpline buttons, a paragraph saying Wysa is not enough and to talk to a person you feel safe with, then Can't make a call? Access these, with Create Safety Plan and Grounding for panic.
takeaway: Be honest that the app is not enough, give named local helplines first, and still offer something to do for people who cannot call.

title: Help is available list
what: Title Help is available, a line for anyone in distress or considering self-harm, and highlighted text These numbers are free, confidential, and available 24/7. A list of named lines each with a Call button, ending with Alan is not suited for crisis situations.
takeaway: Saying free, confidential and 24/7 removes the three worries that stop people calling; each line has a one tap Call.

title: Get help sheet with a call action
what: A lighthouse line drawing, title Get help, a short paragraph on calling the lifeline or a local hotline, and a teal number button that opens the iOS Call sheet.
takeaway: A calm illustration and one big number button make the helpline feel reachable rather than alarming.

title: Slip-up reply without blame
what: Large heading Don't worry about it, then Slip-ups happen and can make you feel bad, but it's crucial not to be too hard on yourself. A Journal Feelings row and a Reset Counter button.
takeaway: Lead with reassurance before any action; the reset is offered after the comfort, not before.

title: Shiny star after a small goal
what: The bird holds a checklist with the speech bubble Tiny task? Done and dusted! over confetti, a smiling star, A Shiny Star for You! and 2 days of Productivity goals done this week! Small steps, strong roots!
takeaway: The mascot speaks in first person and the line praises the size of the step, which suits small daily tasks.

title: Calm goal celebration without confetti
what: Mint background, the bird resting in bushes with a butterfly, bubble Today felt like a soft cloud!, a star, A Shiny Star for You! and You're planting the seeds of a habit! with an Awesome! button.
takeaway: For calm goals the celebration itself is calm: soft colour, a resting pose and a gentle line instead of fireworks.

title: Mascot thanks you for self-care
what: White screen, the bird hugging a heart, bubble Wow! When you take care of yourself, you take care of me, too! Let's do it together, cheep! and a blue pill Lee gained +5.3 Logic, with Next.
takeaway: Framing self-care as shared (you and the companion together) gives warmth without making it about points.

title: It's okay to miss a day
what: The bird carries a mallet with the bubble It's okay to miss a day. The important thing is you're here today, cheep! Below, Repair your 2 day streak? with a free repair offer and Start over.
takeaway: Comfort comes first and praises showing up today; the streak fix is a quiet secondary choice.

title: Sleep coach after a short night
what: Dark screen with 8h 40m Recommended, a bar showing +40m over the 8h baseline, then You could use a little more sleep today. and You need an extra 40 minutes of sleep compared to your baseline.
takeaway: A short night becomes a small concrete ask (40 more minutes) in soft words, not a failing grade.

title: Steady Sleep, Steady Progress
what: Starry purple screen with the serif title Steady Sleep, Steady Progress, then 7 hrs 32 mins of sleep is a solid effort. followed by one note on what more would help, over a 9 hour ring with bed and wake times.
takeaway: A good night gets a short headline that names it as effort, and one line of what could be even better.

title: Fair night with a plain explanation
what: 63 Fair with This was a mixed result that might not leave you feeling fully energised for the day ahead, then What affected your score? with Sleep duration Poor and Sleep quality 4 of 4 in range, and 4h 58m.
takeaway: Explain how the user may feel today and split the cause into what went well and what did not, so a bad night is not all bad.

title: You did it, all habits done
what: A fluffy blue mascot stretching on white, title You did it and Today's positive habits shape your health for tomorrow. with a Claim my reward button.
takeaway: An end of day line that ties today's small acts to tomorrow's health fits a metabolic app well.

title: Great work at 10 check-ins
what: Black screen with a big serif 10, Great work! and You're steadily building a habit of checking in with your emotions. over ten linked rings, each coloured by past moods.
takeaway: Praise the habit of checking in, not the mood itself, so a low day still counts as a good log.

title: See you tomorrow widget
what: Two home widgets with a singing bowl: 1 consecutive day, See you tomorrow! and a week row of ticks with gaps for missed days.
takeaway: Done for the day reads as a friendly goodbye; missed days are simply blank, with no red marks.

title: You stayed with it
what: Big serif 2, You stayed with it! and Your new streak is gaining momentum. Your future self thanks you. over two coloured rings.
takeaway: A small streak is still celebrated in grown up words with no mascot needed.

title: Streak lost (counter example)
what: A grey flame, 1 Day streak lost, an empty week row and Don't give up. Log your meals today to get back on track!
takeaway: Shown as what to avoid: leading with loss and grey empties feels like a penalty, which GoodFlip should not do for mood or sleep.

title: Logging a low mood
what: Weekly insights with flower faces for Sunday and Monday and a plus on today, above I've been planning every day for 3 days in a row.
takeaway: Open on a week of past moods so the new log has a place to land.

title: Logging a low mood
what: A sheet asks How did you feel overall Today? with a soft blue Neutral face and a slider from Very Unpleasant to Very Pleasant.
takeaway: A single slider with a face that changes is quick and needs no words to read.

title: Logging a low mood
what: Slider moved to the far left; the face becomes a frowning purple star labelled Very Unpleasant and the sheet tints purple.
takeaway: The colour and shape change with the mood, so a low mood looks soft, not alarming.

title: Logging a low mood
what: Logged in Wellbeing with the purple star and a card Today, you had a Very Unpleasant day. Logged now, saved to Apple Health.
takeaway: The confirmation states the mood back plainly with no judgement, but offers no support; GoodFlip should add a care line and coach option here.

title: Logging a low mood
what: Daily reflection asks if any of today's three completed tasks played a role, with plus buttons to tag them.
takeaway: A gentle what played a role question turns a low mood into reflection.

title: Logging a low mood
what: Back on weekly insights, Tuesday now shows the purple star beside the earlier flowers; the streak still reads 3 days in a row.
takeaway: A low day still keeps the streak, so logging honestly is never punished.

title: Completing a goal
what: Home with the bird in its room, a 0 / 15 energy bar and 7 goals left for today! with tick buttons for Drink water, Get out of bed and Wash my face.
takeaway: The to do list counts down what is left, not what is missed.

title: Completing a goal
what: After a tick, confetti falls and a toast says You're amazing! First time completion while the list shows 6 goals left.
takeaway: A small toast right on the list confirms the tap without leaving the screen.

title: Completing a goal
what: A full screen forest with the bird, a MAX energy bar and Woohoo!
takeaway: A short full screen moment for the first goal of the day.

title: Completing a goal
what: The same screen adds Lee drank Water and energized for Day 1, a +139 Rainbow Stones pill and Continue.
takeaway: The mascot does the thing with you, which makes the goal feel shared.

title: Completing a goal
what: Green screen 3RD GOAL COMPLETED! with the egg and Woohoo! Your Micropet egg just got one step closer to hatching! and a Reflect link.
takeaway: A Reflect link sits under the celebration so a quiet user can go deeper.

title: Completing a goal
what: Three Stars Earned! with the bird saying Whoa! I'm a checklist champion now! and 6 days of Productivity goals done this week! That's real progress shining through!
takeaway: Weekly praise counts days done, never days missed.

title: Logging sleep
what: Sleep day view reading No data with a Log sleep floating button.
takeaway: An empty day invites a log with one clear button.

title: Logging sleep
what: Log sleep sheet with Bedtime and Wake up, each with Date and Time rows, and Save.
takeaway: Two plain rows, bed and wake, are the simplest manual sleep entry.

title: Logging sleep
what: The bedtime time picker is open on 1:47 PM.
takeaway: Native wheels are familiar but fiddly for older hands; preset chips would be faster.

title: Logging sleep
what: Bedtime changed to 8:00 PM in the picker.
takeaway: Defaults should start near a normal bedtime so fewer scrolls are needed.

title: Logging sleep
what: Both times set, 8:00 PM to 9:47 PM, ready to save.
takeaway: Showing the full range before saving lets the user check it.

title: Logging sleep
what: Back on the day view: 1h 47m of 8h goal with a partly filled ring, bedtime and wake time, and no comment on the short night.
takeaway: Shown as a gap: the result is only a number against a goal. GoodFlip should add one warm line here, different for a short night and a steady one.
